quadratics.description:
Be able to answer any Quadratics question on Paper 1 without notes.

Key points:
• Complete the square and read off the vertex and line of symmetry
• Use the discriminant b² − 4ac for two, one or no real roots
• Solve quadratic inequalities with a sketch
• Solve a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously
• Solve equations that are quadratic in a function of x, e.g. in x² or √x
• Use the discriminant for a line that is tangent to a curve

How: For each key point, rework one example from your notes or textbook, then cover the answer and do it again from memory. Write down any formula you had to look up.

First step: Open your notes on Quadratics and redo one example for the first key point without looking.

mapped.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry (9701), Paper 2
units: Atomic structure: Describe protons, neutrons, electrons and atomic/isotope notation; Write electron configurations using subshells and orbitals
Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry: Calculate relative atomic and molecular masses; Use the mole and Avogadro constant in calculations
Chemical bonding: Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic and covalent species; Explain ionic, covalent, dative covalent and metallic bonding
States of matter: Use the ideal gas equation pV = nRT in calculations; Explain deviations of real gases from ideal behaviour
Chemical energetics: Define enthalpy changes of reaction, formation and combustion; Draw and use energy cycle (Hess's law) diagrams
Electrochemistry: Assign oxidation numbers to elements in compounds and ions; Identify oxidation and reduction in electron-transfer reactions
Equilibria: Explain dynamic equilibrium and the effect of changing conditions; Apply Le Chatelier's principle to predict shifts
Reaction kinetics: Explain rates in terms of collision theory and activation energy; Interpret rate and concentration-time graphs
Chemical periodicity: Describe trends in atomic radius, melting point and conductivity across Period 3; Explain trends in ionisation energy across Period 3
Group 2: Describe trends in atomic radius, melting point and reactivity down the group; Write equations for reactions of Group 2 metals with water, oxygen and acids
Group 17: Describe trends in physical properties of the halogens down the group; Identify halogens and halide ions using displacement and silver nitrate tests
Nitrogen and sulfur: Describe the formation and uses of ammonia; Describe the chemistry of nitrogen oxides as pollutants
Introduction to organic chemistry: Name and draw compounds using IUPAC rules; Identify functional groups and write structural, displayed and skeletal formulae
Hydrocarbons: Describe free-radical substitution of alkanes and its mechanism; Write equations for complete and incomplete combustion of alkanes
Halogen compounds: Describe nucleophilic substitution of halogenoalkanes; Compare SN1 and SN2 mechanisms and rates
Hydroxy compounds: Classify alcohols as primary, secondary or tertiary; Describe oxidation of alcohols and the reagents used
Carbonyl compounds: Describe preparation of aldehydes and ketones; Use Tollens' and Fehling's reagents to distinguish aldehydes and ketones
Carboxylic acids and derivatives: Describe properties and acid strength of carboxylic acids; Write equations for esterification and ester hydrolysis
Nitrogen compounds: Describe preparation and basicity of primary amines; Describe formation of nitriles and hydroxynitriles
Polymerisation: Describe addition polymerisation from alkenes; Draw repeat units from monomers and vice versa
Organic synthesis: Design multi-step routes between given functional groups; Select reagents and conditions for each synthetic step
Analytical techniques: Identify functional groups from infrared absorptions; Interpret mass spectra to find Mr and fragmentation patterns
